title: Terraform module: GPU node groups with ASG + Karpenter support for Private VPC
creator: Leo Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a single Terraform module we can use in Redwood Private installations that provisions GPU-backed node groups with two runtime modes: ASG (AutoScalingGroup + Launch Template) and Karpenter Provisioner. The module must be opinionated for production (taints/tolerations, node labels, drivers, lifecycle hooks, spot fallback) while configurable for customer constraints (instance families, max pod density, GPU vendor).

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Module exposes a clear switch: mode = "asg" | "karpenter".
- ASG path: creates Launch Template, AutoScalingGroup with mixed instances policy (on-demand/spot weights), lifecycle hooks for graceful termination (drain), and CloudWatch alarms for instance health.
- Karpenter path: creates IAM roles, provisioner manifest (templated), and LaunchTemplate-like spec for Karpenter to pick instance types/GPU-family.
- GPU concerns: support nvidia and amd gpu drivers by installing our driver DaemonSet via Helm chart (referenceable), and surface node label gpu.brand = nvidia|amd.
- Node readiness & health checks: integrate EC2/ASG instance status + Kubernetes node Ready gating; expose a Terraform output with remediation playbook link.
- Upgrades: support blue/green-style node replacement for both ASG and Karpenter. Provide a recommended upgrade script that cordons/drains nodes respecting PDBs, checks CSI detach for local NVMe, and validates application-level health before scale-down.
- Observability hooks: annotate nodes for infra metrics; wire a node exporter job and kubelet metrics (we provide example Grafana dashboard urls).
- Tests: integration test in a dedicated Private staging account (small fleet of g4dn.xlarge-like instances) and a fast unit plan/apply test in CI that uses mock variables.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Single module vs two modules: chose single module with "mode" flag to reduce duplication and make rolling upgrades consistent across modes. Adds conditional complexity in the TF code but simplifies usage in private manifests.
- Spot mixing: default is mixed instances with a safety fallback (min_on_demand_pct). This reduces cost but avoids mass eviction risk.
- Driver management: module will not bake drivers into AMIs (we saw AMI drift issues across customer air-gapped environments). Instead we deploy a validated DaemonSet that installs drivers at boot. This supports private deployments where AMI customization is hard.

Interfaces (high level):
- Inputs (selected): mode, cluster_name, subnet_ids, gpu_vendor, gpu_instance_families, desired_capacity_gpu, max_capacity_gpu, min_on_demand_pct, karpenter_provisioner_defaults, node_labels, taints, enable_spot, update_strategy, lifecycle_hooks_enabled, ssh_key_name, iam_instance_profile, custom_user_data.
- Outputs (selected): node_group_id, launch_template_id (if ASG), karpenter_provisioner_name (if Karpenter), iam_role_arn, remediation_runbook_url, last_apply_timestamp.

Security and compliance notes:
- IAM least-privilege role templates included; document required permissions for on-prem/private air-gapped deployments (customer-managed artifact buckets for driver images).
- KMS: module allows KMS key ARNs for launch template encrypted volumes.

Upgrade plan (brief):
1) Bump module version in staging private account.
2) Create canary node pool (10% of GPU capacity) with new AMI/driver combo.
3) Validate workload health for 24h, run perf microbench (latency p95, throughput).
4) If healthy, gradually migrate remaining capacity rolling 20% batches, cordon/drain respecting PDBs.
5) If failure, rollback by scaling up old node group and marking new as unhealthy.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/987654/GPU+Node+Group+Module
- Prototype PR (ASG path): https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/1234
- Karpenter path PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/1271
- Driver DaemonSet chart: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/tree/main/nvidia-driver
- Staging test runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-GPU-Node-Group-Test

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Karpenter in private air-gapped zones may be blocked by node provisioning constraints. Mitigation: provide an offline artifacts bucket pattern and a deployment checklist for customers.
- Risk: GPU driver install fails on certain AMIs. Mitigation: maintain a matrix of validated AMIs and include automated smoke tests in CI that attach a gpu and run nvidia-smi or equivalent.

Next steps and deliverables:
- Finish Karpenter provisioner templating and add unit tests (Aisha).
- Add e2e smoke that boots 1 GPU node and runs driver validation (SRE paired task).
- Finalize remediation_runbook and add to private console docs.

Expected release: runtime-2.3.0 (module v1.0.0) to be promoted to Private customers after staging verification.
